key_insight: Reliable welding-distortion control in large metallic structures requires balancing physics-based accuracy, computational efficiency and application-specific calibration.
engineering_relevance: Design-stage welding sequence optimisation and structural planning offer the strongest opportunities to reduce distortion and costly corrective work.
method: Review prediction and mitigation research from 2000–2025.
Compare thermo-elasto-plastic, inherent-strain, local/global and emerging data-driven models.
Assess design-stage, in-process and post-welding distortion controls.
evidence_signal: Only approximately 10% and 1% of reviewed references address large aluminium and high-strength steel structures, respectively, indicating limited material-specific evidence.
watch_item: No prediction approach transfers universally across structures; scalable deployment remains constrained by calibration, simplifying assumptions and data availability.
paper_title: A review of prediction and control methods on welding-induced distortions in large metallic structures
